description: Cost per correct decision: what it costs this system to be right. The headline number counts only machine-checked (math) grades, so another model opinion can never enter it. Grades that the world own outcome check proves later sit in their own adjacent panels instead of being summed into the headline, because a route decision is graded twice and blending the two would count it twice. Below the headline: per-model and per-decision-type evidence for routing each decision type to the cheapest model that is actually right, correct-rate and cost-over-time views behind the alert rules, and an AI-judge view kept explicitly secondary. Use the decision type, grade source and model selectors to scope any panel. To reconcile against the CLI, set the time range around a single run: the counters are cumulative, so a wide range aggregates every run ever recorded.
title: Gradebook: Cost per Correct Decision

widgets.description: The headline: cost per 1,000 correct decisions, scoped to grade.source = 'math' and to the demo services so it reconciles with `python -m toyworld`. Rendered as a timeseries rather than a single big number for a concrete reason: this SigNoz version does not evaluate builder formulas on the scalar query path a value panel uses, so the same (A/B)*1000 formula that returns 1.507 as a timeseries came back empty as a scalar, and the value panel's nullZeroValues setting rendered that emptiness as a confident 0. A headline that silently reads zero is worse than one that reads a line, so the panel type changed rather than the number being quietly dropped.

widgets.description: The finding this project exists to show, native in SigNoz: every decision type crossed with every model, with the correct count, the number graded and the dollars spent in one row. Sort by correct against cost and read the next_hop rows: three of the cheapest models in the roster each score 20 out of 20 and sit above claude-sonnet-4.6's 19, at a fraction of its cost. Then read the eta_estimate rows, where three models score zero and sonnet scores 19. Derived ratio columns are deliberately absent: this SigNoz version does not evaluate builder formulas on the table/scalar query path (they return n/a), so the raw counts are shown rather than a column that renders empty. Scoped to grade.source = 'math' and to the demo services so it reconciles with `python -m toyworld`.

widgets.description: The first panel on this dashboard driven by the logs signal rather than metrics. Gradebook emits three failure classes as structured WARN logs (budget_guard_tripped, unknown_model_pricing_miss, missing_response_id), each carrying augmentloop.failure.class as an attribute rather than as prose in the message body, so this groups on the attribute and survives any rewording of the warning text. A class with no row has not occurred in the selected window: these are discrete failure events, not a gauge. budget_guard_tripped is the one the committed log-based alert rule watches. Deliberately NOT scoped to the demo services, because a failure anywhere on the stack is worth seeing.
widgets.title: Failure Events by Class (logs signal)

widgets.description: The raw log lines behind the panel beside it. Each record is emitted through the OTLP LoggingHandler bridge while the decision's span is current, so every line carries the trace id and span id of the decision that produced it. The click-through from a failure to its decision works here even though it does not work from a metric data point, because SigNoz drops metric exemplars before ClickHouse (docs/conventions.md section 10.1).
widgets.title: Recent Failure Events (raw log lines)

widgets.description: Why the panels above are scoped. Gradebook is a portable layer whose contract is the emitted telemetry, not its function signatures, and on this stack several independent services already emit through it: the toy world and its deferred-outcome service, a separate media-processing module and its own outcome service, plus example and verification emitters. Each one shows up here with no dashboard change, which is the portability claim being checked rather than asserted. It is also the reason the reconciliation panels pin themselves to the demo services: an unscoped headline silently blends every service on the stack. The test service is excluded per #47.
